questions.question: Who became the first Chief Minister of Manipur belonging to Bharatiya Janata Party?
questions.solution:

• He is a** former football player and journalist** who joined politics in 2002. 
 
 
• He was a member of the Indian National Congress (INC) before** joining the BJP in 2016. **
 
 
 
• He became the **12th ****Chief Minister of Manipur in March 2017**, after the BJP formed a coalition government with other parties.
 
• He has **represented the Heingang Assembly constituency** in the Manipur Legislative Assembly since 2002.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The Bharatiya Jana Sangh, founded in 1951 by Syama Prasad Mookerjee, is where the BJP got its start.
 
• The Jana Sangh combined with a number of other parties to establish the Janata Party following the declaration of a state of emergency in 1977.

• The state has been facing several challenges, such as insurgency, drug trafficking, and ethnic conflicts.
 
 
 
• **Manohar Parrikar **was a prominent BJP leader from Goa who served as the **Chief Minister of Goa from 2000 to 2005** and again from 2012 to 2014.
 
 
• He later **became the Defence Minister of India in 2014** and served in that position until 2017, when he returned to Goa as the Chief Minister.
 
• He **passed **away in **March 2019** due to **pancreatic cancer.**
 
 
 
• **Longjam Thambu Singh** and **Okram Ibobi Singh** are both **former Chief Ministers of Manipur** who **belonged to the INC (Indian National Congress).**

questions.question: 'Maghi' is another name for which of the following festivals of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Makar Sankranti.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Maghi **is the regional name for the **Makar Sankranti** festival, celebrated in **Punjab**, **Haryana**, **Jammu **Division, and **Himachal **Pradesh.
 
• Makar Sankranti is a Hindu festival celebrated in **January (usually January 14** of the Gregorian calendar), marking the **transition of the sun into the zodiac sign of Makara (Capricorn).**
 
 
• It is always celebrated on the **first day of the month of Magha in the Vikrami calendar**.
 
 
 
• The festival is observed in different parts of India with various names such as **Pongal**, **Lohri**, **Uttarayan**, and Magh Bihu.</s

questions.question: Prince Shuddendra Narayan Singh Deo has been awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his contribution to ______ dance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prince Shuddendra Narayan Singh Deo** was awarded the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1963** for his contribution to **Chhau dance.**

 
 
• He was **born **in **1927 **and was the youngest son of the former Maharaja of **Seraikella in Singhbhum district (Now Jharkhand).**​
 
 
 
• He is a well-known exponent of the **Seraikella Chhau style**, which is known for its intricate footwork, graceful hand gestures, and elaborate costumes.
 
• He **led Sri Kalapitha**, the main institution offering instruction in the dance form, and **popularized it across the nation and in Europe.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Chhau is a traditional dance form that originated in the eastern states of India, mainly in Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Odisha.

 
 
• The dance form is known for its acrobatic movements, martial arts, and colorful costumes.
 
• West Bengal and Odisha also have their variations of Chhau, known as Purulia Chhau and Mayurbhanj Chhau, respectively.
 
 
 
• Mohiniyattam and Kathakali are two classical dance forms that originated in Kerala.
 
 
• It is named after 'Mohini', the feminine form of Lord Vishnu, which means 'the dance of Mohini'.​
 
 
 
• Kathakali is a classical dance form of Kerala.
 
 
• It is a highly stylized and ritualistic dance drama that combines elements of ballet, opera, masque, and pantomime.
 
• The performers wear elaborate costumes and makeup to depict characters from Indian mythology.
 
 
 
• Kathak is a classical dance form of North India basically Uttar Pradesh.
 
 
• It is a storytelling dance that involves intricate footwork, spins, and graceful movements of the hands and arms.
 
• The themes of Kathak are often romantic or devotional in nature.​​

questions.question: In _____, the Indian Parliament passed the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is December 2019.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **The Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA)** was **passed **by the Indian Parliament on **December 11, 2019.**
 
• The **Citizenship Amendment Bill (CAA Bill)** was **first introduced in 2016 in Lok Sabha** for amending the Citizenship Act of 1955.
 
 
• A Joint Parliamentary Committee was tasked with reviewing this bill; the committee eventually turned in its findings on January 7, 2019.
 
• On January 8, 2019, the Lok Sabha enacted the Citizenship Amendment Bill, which expired on the same day as the 16th Lok Sabha was dissolved. 
 
 
 
• Amit Shah, the Minister of Home Affairs,** reintroduced** this bill in the **17th Lok Sabha on December 9, 2019**, and it was subsequently **passed in that house on December 10.**
 
 
• On **December 11**, the **Rajya Sabha also approved** the measure. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA) 2019:**
 
• It **amends **the **Citizenship Act of 1955** to **grant citizenship to** six non-Muslim populations (**Hindus**, **Sikhs**, **Buddhists**, **Jains**, **Parsis**, and **Christians**) who **entered India** illegally on or **before December 31, 2014**, on the basis of their faith.
 
 
• These communities **should be from Pakistan, Afghanistan, **and **Bangladesh.**
 
 
 
• Members of the six communities are **released from prosecution under** the **Passport Act of 1920** and the **Foreigners Act of 1946.**
 
• If a person has **lived in India for 11 of the preceding 14 years** and **for the last 12 months**, they are **eligible **under this statute.
 
 
• The period of residency has been shortened from 11 to 5 years for the designated class of undocumented migrants.

questions.question: In which decade did the Green Revolution take place in India?

• It was a **significant success in India**, as it** helped to increase agricultural output** (especially wheat and rice) and reduce food shortages.
 
• However, it also had **some negative impacts**, such as **environmental degradation**, **soil erosion**, and the** loss of traditional farming practices**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****The Green Revolution in India:**

 
• The Green Revolution, which refers to the large-scale introduction of high-yielding varieties of seeds, fertilizers, and pesticides in agriculture, has been criticized for its negative impact on small farmers.
 
• The Government of India launched the Green Revolution in 1965 under the Third Five-Year Plan(1961-66).
 
• MS Swaminathan is considered the father of the Green Revolution in India.
 
• Norman Borlaug is known as the 'Father of Green Revolution' in the world.
 
• In India, the aim of this revolution was to increase the productivity of agricultural crops, particularly wheat and rice.
 
 
• The main focused crops were **Wheat**, **Rice**, **Jowar**, **Bajra **and **Maize**.
 
 
 
• In the first phase of the Green Revolution, the use of HYV seeds was limited to the more prosperous states of Haryana, Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Western Uttar Pradesh.
 
• HYV seeds refer to high-yielding varieties of seeds that were developed during the Green Revolution to increase crop yields.

questions.question: Whom did Udham Singh kill?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Michael O'Dwyer.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Udham Singh** was an Indian revolutionary who **assassinated Michael O'Dwyer in March 1940.**

 
 
• The assassination was carried out as **payback for** O'Dwyer's involvement in the **1919 Jallianwala Bagh massacre in Amritsar**, which Singh personally survived.
 
 
 
• **On December 26, 1899,** in **Lahore**, British India, Udham Singh was **born "Sher Singh"** into a Sikh household.
 
 
• His parents were **Tehal Singh** and **Narain Kaur.**
 
 
 
• Singh was **hung in July 1940** after being found guilty of murder at a later trial.
 
 
• He went by the** name "Ram Mohammad Singh Azad"** while he was detained, signifying his opposition to colonialism and the three main Indian religions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Michael O'Dwyer **served as an Irish colonial official in the **Indian Civil Service (ICS)** before becoming the **Lieutenant Governor of Punjab** in British India from **1913 to 1919.**

 
 
• During O'Dwyer's tenure as Punjab's Lieutenant Governor, the **Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred in Amritsar on April 13, 1919.**
 
 
 
• On **April 13, 1919**, many locals came to the park to celebrate **Baisakhi**. There was a carnage known as the** Amritsar Carnage or Jallianwala Bagh Massacre.**
 
 
• The demonstrators also aimed to peacefully oppose the apprehension and expulsion of two prominent national figures,** Satyapal** and **Saifuddin Kitchlew.**
 
 
• The incident resulted in the deaths of hundreds of people and sparked outrage across India.
 
 
 
• **Brigadier R.E.H. Dyer (General Dyer)**, an Anglo-Indian at the time, **gave the order for the Gurkha British Indian** army to carry it out.
 
 
 
• **Sydney Roullete/Rowlatt** was an Anglo-Egyptian **judge **who **presided **over a **Sedition Committee** appointed in **1917 **by the British Indian Government to evaluate political terrorism in India.
 
 
• Based on the **Rowlatt Committee's report**, the **Rowlatt Act (Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919)** was passed, which authorized the **arrest, for 2 years without trial**, of any person suspected of terrorism living in British India.
 
 
 
• **John Simon** was a **British politician** who held senior Cabinet posts from the beginning of the First World War to the end of the Second World War.
 
 
• He was **appointed Chairman** of the** Simon Commission (the Indian Statutory Commission) in 1927.**
 
• The **Commission** was a** group of seven British Members of Parliament** and was supposed to** investigate the workings of the Government of India Act of 1919 **and suggest improvements to the system.
 
• The **3rd of February 1928** saw the **arrival of the Simon Commission in Bombay.** The nation as a whole persisted in boycotting the commission the same day.

questions.question: Which of the following Chinese pilgrims visited India about 50 years after Xuan Tsang?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** I-king.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **I-king/sing**, also known as **Yijing**, was a Chinese Buddhist monk who **visited India around 50 years after Xuan Tsang.**
 
• He sailed from Canton to **India **in 671 and **arrived **there in **673**. Following his tour of the holy Buddhist sites in Magadha.
 
• He spent **10 years** studying the Vinya at the illustrious **Nalanda monastery (676–685)**.
 
• In 685, he departed from India and went to the then heavily Indianized city of **Shri Bhoja** (or Sri Boja, also called Shri Vijaya, or Palembang in **Sumatra**). Here, he focused on **translating Buddhist scriptures** written in Sanskrit.
 
• **He went back to China in 689** to get help with his translations. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Xuan Tsang/Hyun Tsang or Hiuen-Tsang** was a famous Chinese Buddhist monk who** visited India in the 7th century AD.**

 
 
• He left China in AD** 629 **and traveled via Central Asia via Kucha on the northern trade route to **reach northern India.**
 
• There, in the **city of Kanauj**, he was the guest of the renowned Indian** ruler Harsavardhana.**
 
• His journey lasted for** 17 years**, during which he visited many important Buddhist centers and monasteries.
 
• He **returned **to China in AD **645**.
 
 
 
• **Fahiyan/Fa-hien**, also known as **Faxian**, was another Chinese Buddhist monk who** visited India in the 5th century AD**.
 
 
• He travelled to India during **Chandragupta II’s rule** and composed the** book Fo-kwo-ki **(Travels of Fa-hien).
 
• He was the first Chinese Buddhist pilgrim to leave an account of his travels to Central Asia, India, and Sri Lanka. 
 
• He is known for his detailed account of the Buddhist sites and teachings in India, which he recorded in his** book "A Record of Buddhist Kingdoms."**
 
 
 
• **Tsang Hi** was a **Chinese general** who lived during the **Tang dynasty**, while** Lao Tzu** was a **Chinese philosopher** who lived during the **Zhou dynasty.**

questions.question: How many minutes is the duration of a Kabaddi match?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**40 minutes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kabaddi **is a popular contact sport in South Asia.
 
• It is played between two teams of** 7 players each.**
 
• The objective of the game is for a player, known as a raider, to cross into the opposing team's half and tag as many defenders as possible before returning to their own half.
 
• A match consists of **two halves**, each **lasting 20 minutes (total 40 minutes)**, with a **break of 5 minutes in between.**
 
• Kabaddi is also **known **as **hu-tu-tu in western India**, **ha-do-do in eastern India and Bangladesh**, **chedu-gudu in southern India**, **gudu in Sri Lanka**, and** theechub in Thailand.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Time duration for different sports:**

 
 

 **Sports**
 **Common Regulation time duration (in minutes)**
 **Details**
 
 

 Football
 90 ( 2 halves of 45 minutes)
 15-minute rest period in between called halftime.
 
 

 Field Hockey
 60 ( 4 quarters of 15 minutes)
 2 minutes break after the first and third quarter and a 15 minutes-interval after the second quarter, which is halftime.
 
 

 Kabaddi
 40 ( two halves of 20 minutes)
 A 5 minutes break between halves.
 
 

 Basketball
 48 ( four quarters of 12 minutes)
 2.5 minutes break after the first and third quarter and a 15 minutes-interval after the second quarter, which is halftime.
 
 

 Boxing
 4 to 12 rounds of 3 minutes each.
 
 
 

 Freestyle wrestling
 6 ( 2 periods of 3 minutes)
 30 seconds break in between.

questions.question: Three of the following four are ecological pyramids, and thus form a group. Which does not belong to this group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**pyramid of culture.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **pyramid of culture** is not an ecological pyramid as it does not represent any ecological parameter in an ecosystem.

 
 
• It is a term **used to describe the hierarchical structure of human societies or organizations.**
 
 
 
• The **pyramid of energy**, the **pyramid of biomass**, and the **pyramid of numbers** are **ecological pyramids** that represent the flow of energy, the amount of biomass, and the number of organisms at each trophic level in an ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
A **graphical representation** of the **relationships between various living things at various trophic levels** is called an **ecological pyramid.**

 
 
• 
 
The pyramid of numbers is a notion created by **Charles Elton**. The **pyramid of energy or productivity**, was later created by **Raymond Lindeman **and **G. Evelyn Hutchinson.**

 
 
• 
 
It is evident that these pyramids resemble real pyramids, with the **broadest base**—covered by the** lowest trophic level, or producers**—at the base.

 
 
• 
 
The primary consumers and other members of the following trophic level occupy the level after them.

 
 
 
 
• **Pyramid of energy** represents the **amount of energy transferred from one trophic level to another** in an ecosystem.
 
 
• It shows that only a small fraction of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next, resulting in a decrease in the amount of energy available at higher trophic levels.
 
• It is **always upright **as the **energy flow in a food chain** is **always unidirectional.**
 
 
 
• **Pyramid of biomass** represents the **amount of living or organic matter present at each trophic level** in an ecosystem.
 
 
• It shows that the biomass decreases at higher trophic levels as a result of the loss of energy through respiration and other metabolic processes.
 
• It is **also upright except** for that **observed in oceans** where large numbers of **zooplanktons depend on** a relatively **smaller number of phytoplankton.**
 
 
 
• **Pyramid of numbers** represents the **number of individuals present at each trophic level** in an ecosystem.
 
 
• It shows that the number of individuals decreases at higher trophic levels as a result of the loss of energy and competition for resources.
 
• It is** usually upright, except** for some situations like the **detritus food chain**, where many organisms feed on one dead plant or animal.

questions.question: ______ is the custodian of the country's foreign exchange reserves and is vested with the responsibility of managing their investments.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Reserve Bank of India (RBI) 

__
 
• It is India’s central bank.
 
• In compliance with the terms of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• It was founded on April 1, 1935, in Calcutta.
 
 
• It was permanently moved to Mumbai in 1937.
 
 
 
• Though originally privately owned, since nationalisation in 1949, the Reserve Bank is fully owned by the Government of India.
 
• The** foreign exchange reserves are solely under its custody.**
 
• It is also vested with the responsibility of managing their investments.
 
• It regulates the issue of Bank notes and the keeping of reserves with a view to securing monetary stability in India and generally operating the currency and credit system of the country to its advantage.
 
• It also monitors monetary policies through its Monetary Policy Committee (MPC).​​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**State Bank of India:**

 
• The Imperial Bank of India was nationalised to **establish the State Bank of India on July 1, 1955.**
 
• It is the **biggest public-sector bank** in India.
 
• Its first chairman was John Mathai.
 
• Its **present chairman** is **Dinesh Kumar Khara.**
 
• It administers public debt, acts as the government's bank, and collects money and makes payments on the government's behalf.
 
• It **lends money to commercial banks** and takes deposits from them.
 
• It acts as a **representative for cooperative banks.**

questions.question: How many field umpires are there in a cricket match?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Field Umpires:**

 
• **Two field umpires** are chosen, **one for the bowlers' end and one for the strikers' end**, to oversee the game.
 
• They will choose places from which they may readily observe any action that may necessitate their decision.
 
• After one inning for each team, the umpires will switch ends.
 
• The **striker's end umpire can decide to stand** either on the off side or the leg side of the pitch by informing the captain of the fielding side, the striker, and the other umpire.​</strong

questions.question: What proportion of the proposed jobs has been reserved for women as per the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one third.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA):

__
 
• The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) was enacted by the Central Government of India in the year 2005.
 
• It mandates that **women** must receive priority in order for them to make up **at least one-third of the beneficiaries.**
 
• Established by the Ministry of Rural Development.
 
• MGNREGA is one of the biggest labor guarantee programs globally.
 
• The main goal of the program is to provide adult members of rural households who are willing to perform unskilled manual labor related to public work with 100 days of employment guaranteed per fiscal year.
 
• The legally-backed guarantee that any adult living in a rural area would find a job within 15 days of requesting it, or else an "unemployment allowance" must be provided, is the most significant aspect of the MGNREGA framework.
 
• By giving women equal pay for equal labour, MGNREGA has been successful in lowering poverty, raising the standard of living in rural households, and empowering them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Right to Work:

 
• It is not specifically acknowledged as a fundamental right in the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is unenforceable in a court of law because it is included in Part IV of the Constitution (Directive Principles of State Policy) under Article 41.
 
• According to Article 41 of the Constitution, “the State shall within the limits of its economic capacity and development, make effective provision for securing the right to work, to education and to public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement, and in other cases of undeserved want.”

questions.question: During whose tenure among the following the Swarn Singh Committee was formed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indira Gandhi.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Indira Gandhi:**

__
 
• She was the **first female prime minister **of India and the **second **with the **longest tenure**.
 
• She joined as a member of the Congress's Working Committee in 1955.
 
• She declared the **nationalization of banks **in India on July 19, 1969.
 
• She was instrumental in the enactment of the **26th Amendment **to the Indian Constitution, which **abolished the Privy Purse **and **nullified Articles 291 and 362**.
 
• She took a strong decision to stand by the Bangladeshi people throughout the Liberation War.
 
• She was **awarded the Bharat Ratna** in 1972.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Morarji Desai:**

 
• He is the **Finance Minister** **who** has so far **submitted the most budgets.**
 
• He served as the prime minister of India from March 24, 1977, to July 28, 1979.
 
• He was the** first prime minister of India** to be elected **without being a member of the Indian National Congress**.
 
• In addition, at the age of 81, he became the **oldest prime minister** in history.
 
• He reopened ties with China, which had been halted since a 1962 border conflict.
 
• He **made it harder** for any government **to declare a national emergency **in the future.

**Manmohan Singh:**

 
• He was India's prime minister from 2004 until 2014.
 
• He holds the position of India's **third-longest serving prime minister**.
 
• He worked with the Planning Commission that created the five-year plans.
 
• He was appointed as the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India in 1982.He was appointed as the University Grants Commission (UGC) Chairman in 1991.
 
• The **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act** was put into effect in 2005 under his tenure.
 
• His government **instituted Value Added Tax (VAT), **a more streamlined and uniform tax system,** to replace the Sales Tax.**

**​Swarn Singh Committee:**

 
• It was created **to give recommendations** regarding **fundamental duties**.
 
• It **suggested** **adding a section **on fundamental duties **to the Constitution.**
 
• Its recommendations were enacted through the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (Article 51A)** in 1976.

 
• The list of Fundamental Duties as mentioned in the Article 51A:

 
 

 
 
S.No.

 
 
 
Fundamental Duties

 
 
 

 
 
1.

 
 
 
Abide by the Indian Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem

 
 
 

 
 
2.

 
 
 
Cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom

 
 
 

 
 
3.

 
 
 
Uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India

 
 
 

 
 
4.

 
 
 
Defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so

 
 
 

 
 
5.

 
 
 
Promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities and to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women

 
 
 

 
 
6.

 
 
 
Value and preserve the rich heritage of the country’s composite culture

 
 
 

 
 
7.

 
 
 
Protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife and to have compassion for living creatures

 
 
 

 
 
8.

 
 
 
Develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform

 
 
 

 
 
9.

 
 
 
Safeguard public property and to abjure violence

 
 
 

 
 
10.

 
 
 
Strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement

 
 
 

 
 
11.

 
 
 
Provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years.

questions.question: Who chooses the Speaker of the Lok Sabha?

options.text: Only members of the Lok Sabha from the ruling party

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All members of Lok Sabha.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ ****Speaker of the Lok Sabha:**

 
• **Article 93 **of the Constitution provides for the **election of the Speaker **and the Deputy Speaker.
 
• He or she needs to be a House member.
 
• He or she is **elected **from among the members of the Lok Sabha by a **simple majority of all members **present and voting.
 
• His term in office is five

questions.question: Which folk dance of Punjab is mainly performed by women?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Giddha.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Giddha**:

__
 
• It is a well-liked folk dance performed by females in the **Punjab **area.
 
• It is **distinct **from other types of Punjabi traditional dance.
 
• It is not necessary to perform the two-headed barrel dhol drum.
 
• It **depicts **the histories of women's lives, encompassing **domestic life, marriage, and homesickness.**
 
• Other **Punjab folk dances **are:
 
 
• Bhangra.
 
• Luddi.
 
• Kikkli.
 
• Sammi.
 
• Gatka(Dankara).
 
• Jhumar.
 
• Jaago.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Jawara**:

 
• It is performed by both **men and women**.
 
• It is a **Madhya Pradesh** folk dance.
 
• It is mostly done by the peasant communities in the **Bundelkhand region.** 
 
• It is one of the harvest dances in the region.
 
• Other **Madhya Pradesh folk dances **include:
 
 
• Matki.
 
• Aada.
 
• Khada Nach.
 
• Phulpati.
 
• rida Dance.
 
• Selalarke.
 
• Selabhadoni.
 
• Maanch.
 
 

**Dadra**:

 
• It is a folk dance from **Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• It is performed by courtesans.
 
• It is mainly a **celebration of marriage **and physical pleasures.
 
• Other **folk dances in Uttar Pradesh **are:
 
 
• Charkula.
 
• Kajri.
 
• Kathak.
 
• Khyal.
 
• Nautanki.
 
• Ramlila.
 
• Raslila.
 
 

**Fugdi**:

 
• It is a folk dance **from Goa and Maharashtra**.
 
• It is **performed by women **of tribal, Hindu, and Christian communities.
 
• It is performed with the sounds of women clapping.
 
• List of **folk dances in Goa and Maharashtra**:
